text:
emerald-support: :rotating_light: Hi team — Emerald Clinic here. We signed the HIPAA/BAA addendum last month but noticed audit logs for their PHI-accessing endpoints are missing starting after a KMS key rotation on 2026-02-28. This is urgent for their upcoming audit, can you advise?

alyssa (support): Thanks for flagging. Can you paste an example of a request ID and approximate time range where logs are missing? Also confirm whether they’re on hosted or private (VPC) deployment.

emerald-support: Request IDs: req_8f3a2b, req_8f3a9d, timestamps around 2026-02-28 03:12–03:30 UTC. They’re on hosted API (paid tenant) but using a customer-managed KMS key alias: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/emerald-prod-key. BAA signed 2025-11-02.

jordan (eng-runtime): Got it. Quick check: are you seeing API 401s or 5xxs when calling the API after rotation, or do calls succeed but audit events not appear in console?

emerald-support: Calls succeeded for most requests — client saw occasional 401s for a few minutes during rotation. But the audit export shows a gap — those specific EHR read actions (route /v1/patient/records) have no entries from 03:12–03:30.

meena (security): Looping in security. We need the raw request headers (sanitized) and one full correlated event for a missing entry. Please include x-request-id, date, and server request-id. If you can’t paste headers here, upload to the secure s3 link I just DM’d.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-4122 (emerald-clinic audit gap). Assignee: alyssa. Priority: P1.

alyssa (support): Repro steps request: 1) curl to the same tenant with an API key that previously worked 2) call the /v1/patient/records endpoint with patient id 3245 3) note x-request-id in response, 4) check Audit -> Events filtered by request id. Can you run and paste the curl and response headers?

emerald-support: Running now — output below (sanitized):
```
> curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\n  -H "x-request-id: req_8f3a9d" \\n  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/patient/records?patient_id=3245
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 03:15:14 GMT
Server-Request-Id: srv-442aa1
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 118

{ "patient": { ... } }
```

emerald-support: But when I query the Audit export for srv-442aa1 or req_8f3a9d, nothing returns.

jordan (eng-runtime): Two possibilities: 1) audit ingestion briefly failed during KMS rotation (signing/encryption error) or 2) events were written but the Audit UI query layer failed to surface them (indexing lag). I’ll check ingestion logs for that time range.

meena (security): Also need to confirm whether audit records are encrypted with customer KMS key. If the key was rotated and new key version re-encrypted events differently, our search service might need access to the new key alias policy. @jordan can you verify KMS access logs and if the search/index service had permission to decrypt at rotation time?

jordan (eng-runtime): Pulling logs. Quick note: search service uses a dedicated role redwood-audit-indexer@account that must have kms:Decrypt on key alias "alias/emerald-prod-key". If key policy was overwritten during rotation, that could explain missing results.

sam (solutions): Customer says their cloud team performed rotation via AWS console and selected "create new key" then re-pointed alias. They did not paste the key policy JSON back. Sounds like policy might not include our indexer role.

alyssa (support): Emerald — can you confirm who in your team rotated the key and whether they updated the key policy? If not, can you add redwood-audit-indexer@123456789012 to the key policy or share IAM principal so we can request temporary access?

emerald-support: Confirmed: rotation done by infra@emeraldclinic. They used the console default policy. They did not add our indexer role. They can update the key policy now if that will restore visibility.

meena (security): If the key policy change is the cause, adding our indexer principal and then triggering a re-index should surface the events. However, we need to be careful: customer-managed KMS key access is sensitive under BAA. We require a signed consent form for us to request or modify key policy on their behalf. Can the customer perform the policy update?

emerald-support: They can update immediately. What exact statement do you need in the key policy?

jordan (eng-runtime): Add a KeyPolicy statement with Effect: Allow, Principal: arn:aws:iam::REDFWOOD_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-audit-indexer, Action: ["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"], Resource: *. Example snippet I can DM. After update, run: 
```
# trigger reindex job for tenant
POST https://console.redwood.example.com/internal/audit/reindex
Body: { "tenant_id": "emerald-tenant-42", "start_ts": "2026-02-28T03:00:00Z", "end_ts": "2026-02-28T04:00:00Z" }
```

sam (solutions): Also note retention config: customer was on a non-default retention of 365 days. Nothing should be deleted. This looks like an ingestion/access issue not retention.

emerald-support: They just updated key policy (confirmed) and added principal. They want us to confirm before running reindex.

meena (security): Confirmed — safe to proceed, the policy only grants decrypt/describe to our indexer role. No additional privileges. We should capture audit actions for the reindex job itself. Please schedule during maintenance window.

alyssa (support): I’ve kicked off reindex job for tenant in staging window now — job id reidx-2026-emerald-01. Will post status.

ops-bot: Job reidx-2026-emerald-01 started at 2026-02-28T04:10:00Z. ETA ~8m.

alyssa (support): Job finished. Partial success: 98% indexed. The missing req_8f3a9d and srv-442aa1 are now present in Audit UI. emerald-support, can you confirm you can see entries for the earlier times?

emerald-support: Confirmed — entries visible for 03:12–03:30 now, including server-request-id srv-442aa1. Thank you.

meena (security): Follow-ups: 1) We need to document the KMS key policy requirements in the BAA addendum appendix for customer-managed keys. 2) Add a preventative check to revalidate indexer decrypt permissions when a customer-managed key is rotated. Filing a follow-up ticket.

jordan (eng-runtime): Filed ENG-SEC-1267 to add permission validation on rotation events. Also adding an alert if audit ingestion detects >1m gaps in events tied to KMS errors.

alyssa (support): Closing incident #INC-2026-4122 after customer confirmation. Emerald — I'll send the playbook we used and the sample key policy snippet. If you want, we can also schedule a review session to walk your infra team through safe rotation steps. :thumbsup:

emerald-support: Appreciate it — yes please share playbook and we’ll schedule review. Thanks everyone. (reaction :heart:)

meena (security): Added required language to BAA appendix draft and sent to contracts for sign-off. Marking compliance follow-up.

alyssa (support): Closing thread.
